articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Proposes Demolition of Seven Blocks in Lower Falinge
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, paving the way for 270 new homes and improved public spaces.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has proposed the demolition of seven blocks of flats in the Lower Falinge estate, aiming to construct 270 new homes. The blocks identified for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zeburgh, and Vaynor, which currently contain 150 homes. RBH has stated that these 1970s blocks are no longer fit for purpose and have exceeded their lifespan.

The redevelopment plan is expected to provide a net gain of 150 homes, despite previous demolitions of other blocks in the area, including Waverley, Exbury, Yarwell, and Abbeydale. In addition to the new housing, RBH has committed to enhancing public spaces and improving connectivity to Rochdale town centre through the addition of cycle lanes and footpaths. The majority of the new homes will be built on the land currently occupied by the blocks slated for demolition, with additional plots identified on adjacent land recently acquired by RBH.

Before submitting an official planning application to Rochdale Council, RBH has prepared an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to address potential environmental and social effects of the proposed development. This assessment will consider factors such as noise and dust from demolition, construction traffic, and pollution risks. The EIA is part of RBH's ongoing efforts to ensure responsible development in the area, which has faced significant challenges over the years.

The Lower Falinge estate has been the focus of regeneration efforts for over a decade. It was identified as the most deprived area in England for five consecutive years starting in 2013. In 2016, former Prime Minister David Cameron referred to it as a 'sink estate', highlighting the severe social and economic issues faced by residents. Currently, only the Zeburgh block remains occupied, with residents campaigning against the demolition. However, the campaign has struggled to gain traction due to the low number of remaining residents in the affected blocks. RBH has indicated that they are reviewing feedback from recent consultations before proceeding with the planning application, expected to be submitted in early autumn.

articles.title: Full house for National Emergency Briefing screening in Falinge
articles.excerpt: A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with Rochdale councillors Tricia Ayrton and Shah Wazir joining residents for the event and discussion afterwards.
articles.content_html:
A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with two Rochdale Council portfolio holders joining residents for the event and subsequent discussion.

Organisers have thanked everyone who attended the screening, saying it was encouraging to see such a strong turnout for the film and the conversation which followed.

Rochdale Borough Council portfolio holders Councillor Tricia Ayrton and Councillor Shah Wazir were among those attending.

Organisers thanked both councillors for remaining after the screening to listen to residents, take part in discussions and consider how the issues raised by the film could be discussed more widely.

They said the councillors left the event with a plan to help ensure the film and its message reach a broader audience.

The National Emergency Briefing brings together scientists, campaigners and public figures to discuss climate change and the risks they believe the UK faces, with contributors associated with the project including environmental campaigner Chris Packham.

The Falinge event gave residents an opportunity not only to watch the presentation together but to discuss its arguments and what they could mean at a local level.

Following the strong turnout, another community screening has already been arranged.

The next screening will take place on Thursday, September 4 at 6pm, giving residents who were unable to attend the latest event another opportunity to see the film and join the discussion.

Organisers thanked residents, guests and councillors for supporting the event and helping create what they described as an important community conversation.
